summary: Live OMS exit path. Scope: 4 files, 433/69, one commit, one recognised agent marker, author krshk30 != reviewer claude-1. THE DEFECT IS REAL AND I CONFIRMED IT ON THE BOX INDEPENDENTLY: NUR armed at 16:34:02 UTC = 12:34:02 ET on BOTH legs while both were FLAT (the prior NUR rows, live:orb and live:schwab_1m_v2, both closed at 12:06:18 ET); new rows opened 13:29:45.887 and 13:29:46.159 ET; CW_FLIP exits fired at 17:29:47.732 and 17:29:50.316 UTC = 13:29:47 and 13:29:50 ET. A decision made while flat survived 55 minutes and sold a position 1 to 4 seconds after it opened. CENSUS DENOMINATORS RE-DERIVED, not accepted: zgrep of oms_v2_managed_exit:CW_FLIP across ALL 23 retained oms logs gives live:orb 12 and live:schwab_1m_v2 7, total 19 gradeable, matching the stated 4/7 and 7/12 exactly; a plain grep returns 4 because the rotated logs are gzipped, so the denominator is only reachable with zgrep. CONTROLLED PAIR over the CALL-GRAPH population (75 test files reaching OmsRiskService / oms.service / cw_flip, selected by call graph rather than by symbol name after the #921 lesson), pristine worktrees: base c47d3a76 = 1160 passed / 0 failed / 1 xfailed; head = 1166 passed / 0 failed / 1 xfailed; +6 = the six new tests. EIGHT OWN MUTATIONS in a worktree separate from the suite run, each ast.parse-checked, control green before and after. NOTE the first attempt was VOID: zsh does not word-split an unquoted variable holding two paths, so pytest reported 'no tests ran'; re-run with explicit paths. RED, confirming codex's four claims independently: (1) expiry 180.0 -> 86400.0 => test_cw_flip_decision_expires_before_it_can_act; (2) row-identity comparison removed => test_cw_flip_decision_refuses_a_replacement_position; (3) position-opened-after-bar refusal removed => test_cw_flip_refuses_a_position_opened_after_the_decision_bar; (4) arm even with no bound row => test_C3_GTE_1624_webull_ALREADY_CLOSED_emits_NOTHING. OPPOSITE DIRECTION, the control that matters most: (5) force every decision to read as a different position => 9 RED including test_cw_flip_decision_still_executes_for_its_own_position, so the fix DISCRIMINATES rather than disables the ATR exit. REVIEW FOCUS 1 CONFIRMED: 180.0 does match MAX_BAR_AGE_SECONDS_FOR_EMIT = 180.0 at schwab_1m_v2.py:70, which is the gate applied to this exact emit path at :2329 against the same bar.timestamp_ms field, and :2369 already uses the identical 0 <= age <= horizon form. FOCUS 2 CONFIRMED by mutations 3 and 4 plus 2. FOCUS 3 CONFIRMED by mutation 5. FOCUS 4 CONFIRMED: test_C1_AAOG asserts each leg carries its own managed_row_id and the real read is account-scoped via get_open_managed_position(broker_account_name=acct). Also verified independently from the box that bar_time_ms is the bar START, so bar_close = bar_time_ms + 60_000 is correct: 2743 of 2743 schwab_1m_v2 bars in the last 24h are second-aligned to :00 and none has bar_time after its own created_at. Ruff clean; both CI validate runs pass. FOUR FINDINGS, none blocking, all with a green mutation as evidence rather than an opinion. FN1, the strongest: the two 180.0 horizons are UNCOUPLED. Mutating MAX_BAR_AGE_SECONDS_FOR_EMIT to 300.0 while leaving _V2_CW_FLIP_MAX_BAR_AGE_SECONDS at 180.0 leaves all 1166 tests GREEN, so the OMS comment's claim to 'match the strategy's existing live-bar freshness horizon' is enforced by nothing. The silent failure is asymmetric: raise the strategy horizon and every flip emitted in the gap is refused by the OMS as invalid_or_expired_bar, i.e. the ATR flip exit stops happening. oms/service.py:60 ALREADY imports from project_mai_tai.strategy_core, so importing the constant is a one-line fix. FN2: the downstream 'no open row -> drop any stale flip' guard lost its only test in the C3 rewrite. Deleting that _clear_cw_flip_pending call leaves all 1166 GREEN. The old C3 asserted it through _drive_exit(..., snapshot=None) and also asserted no phantom sell was emitted; the rewrite moved the assertion upstream to acceptance-time refusal and nothing replaced the downstream one. The guard is still in the code and still commented as load-bearing. FN3: the bar-start-versus-close boundary is unpinned. Removing the + 60_000 leaves all 1166 GREEN. The constant is correct today, measured above, but nothing protects it against a bar-interval or feed-stamping change. FN4: _cw_flip_bound_managed_position fails CLOSED on any DB read exception and _run_db has no retry, so a transient DB fault at ingest now means the ATR flip exit silently does not arm for that leg. Arming was previously a pure in-memory set-add that could not fail. It logs .exception only and nothing pages. Fail-closed is the right default here; the gap is that the miss is unmeasurable. Pin does not deploy; this still requires operator GO.
